features.name: Academic attainment
features.description: The level of formal technical education or advanced academic preparation the applicant presents.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree, equivalent, or no advanced degree is presented.
Master's degree is presented.
Doctoral degree is presented.

features.name: Agentic systems architecture
features.description: The extent of hands-on design or implementation experience with agent-based systems, including control boundaries, guardrails, and supporting infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agent-based tooling experience is shown.
The letter mentions agents or autonomous workflows only in general terms.
The letter describes a recognizable agent architecture, typically pairing Python agents with Go services.
The letter shows deliberate control design for agents, such as permissions, auditability, bounded actions, or explicit end-to-end ownership.

features.name: Algorithmic problem solving
features.description: Practical command of data structures and algorithms as demonstrated through concrete system improvements or redesigns.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Claims strong data-structure or algorithm knowledge, but without a concrete example.
Gives at least one concrete example of improving a system through better algorithm or data-structure choice.
Uses a specific, nontrivial example to show strong algorithmic judgment and a meaningful systems improvement.

features.name: Applied AI production maturity
features.description: Whether the applicant has shipped AI or LLM-backed functionality in real systems and handled reliability, evaluation, or failure modes responsibly.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
Mentions AI or LLM exposure without concrete deployment detail.
Describes shipped AI features or workflows in production.
Describes shipped AI work plus evaluation, hardening, guardrails, or trustworthiness practices.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Whether the letter frames security as enabling internal engineers through usable tooling, secure defaults, empathy, and collaboration rather than policing.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Engineering rigor
features.description: Whether the letter signals maintainability, correctness, testing, reliability, and long-term operational care in engineering work.

levels.descriptor: Shows little sign of care for maintainability, testing, or long-term operation.
Mentions maintenance or correctness only generically.
Explicitly emphasizes dependable systems, careful engineering, or maintainer habits.
Shows multiple reinforcing signals such as typed or tested tooling, careful releases, production standards, or pride in quiet reliability.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: How much the letter substantiates claims with concrete technical examples, mechanisms, scope, or measurements.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on generic claims, requirement-matching language, or buzzwords.
Mixes broad claims with a few specifics, leaving important claims under-evidenced.
Backs most major claims with concrete examples, mechanisms, or outcomes.
Is densely specific enough that the reader can clearly picture what the applicant built and why it mattered.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: How central and substantial Go appears in the applicant's production backend experience.

levels.descriptor: Go is missing, unclear, or only incidental.
Go is mentioned as a language used, but not as a main vehicle for work.
Go is clearly presented as the primary or day-to-day language.
Go is central to multiple production systems or explicitly tied to backend or security-infrastructure ownership.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: How clearly the letter explains the outcomes or practical effects of the applicant's work.

levels.descriptor: Lists tasks with no visible outcomes.
Hints at benefit but remains mostly activity-based.
States clear outcomes such as reduced manual work, faster systems, or fewer bugs.
Shows strong leverage language, tying work to capacity, attention saved, or meaningful organizational effect.

features.name: Narrative quality
features.description: Whether the letter has a coherent, memorable voice and narrative flow rather than reading like a generic checklist.

levels.descriptor: Reads as flat, list-like, or heavily templated prose.
Is competent and readable, but largely generic in voice.
Has a noticeable hook, framing device, or coherent personal story.
Has a strong, memorable voice that reinforces fit without sacrificing substance.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Ongoing attacker-minded practice outside routine product work, especially through capture-the-flag or similar exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional or casual CTF participation or similar practice.
The letter shows regular CTF participation or sustained offensive practice.
The letter shows strong competitive results or especially serious, ongoing offensive-security practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Responsibility for public or external codebases through contribution, maintenance, releases, or user support.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution is mentioned.
Mentions occasional upstream fixes or small patches.
Shows regular contribution behavior, such as repeatedly patching dependencies or contributing upstream when issues are found.
Shows maintainer-level ownership with reviews, releases, community support, or a project used beyond the applicant's team.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: The technical ambition, seriousness, and follow-through of self-directed projects outside formal work.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or simple side project with limited technical stretch.
Describes a substantial side project with nontrivial systems or reliability concerns.
Describes an ambitious systems project that tackles distributed systems, storage, recovery, consensus, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Whether the applicant is motivated by foundational platform or infrastructure work whose benefits compound across many teams.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention foundational leverage or broader organizational impact.
Expresses a general desire for scale or impact but without a clear platform orientation.
Explicitly wants infrastructure or foundational work that benefits many teams.
Repeatedly frames motivation around downstream leverage, central-platform responsibility, or quiet improvements inherited across an organization.

features.name: Production delivery scope
features.description: The breadth and depth of concrete responsibility the applicant describes for testing, launching, maintaining, or operating production systems.

levels.descriptor: Only one or two launched or maintained services are mentioned, or the scope is vague.
Roughly three or four services are mentioned, showing repeated production ownership.
Five or more services are mentioned, with explicit launch, maintenance, or testing responsibility.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: How substantive and production-oriented the applicant's Python experience appears.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or appears only incidentally.
Python is mentioned as a tool or companion language, but depth is unclear.
The letter shows regular production Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is portrayed as a major production language with broad, concrete use across services, automation, and agent behavior.

features.name: Relevant software tenure
features.description: The amount or maturity of directly relevant professional software-engineering experience the applicant claims, often expressed through years of work.

levels.descriptor: Less than 2 years of clearly relevant experience, or tenure is not stated.
About 2 to 3 years of relevant experience; clears the minimum but is still early-career for this role.
About 4 to 5 years of relevant experience; solid mid-level tenure.
6 or more years of relevant experience; deep tenure for this opening.

features.name: Role-specific fit
features.description: How specifically and coherently the letter connects the applicant's background and motivations to this exact role and its stated requirements.

levels.descriptor: Shows little role-specific motivation beyond wanting a software job or a brand-name employer.
Mentions security, scale, or Google in broad terms without a strong personal rationale.
Gives a clear role-relevant reason for interest, such as secure-by-default tooling or scaling scarce security effort.
Presents a precise, memorable thesis for wanting this role that is tightly tied to the team's mandate and the applicant's own priorities.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Hands-on experience assessing systems for security weaknesses and validating remediation.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Mentions security reviews or assessments only in general terms.
Describes concrete assessment work such as threat models, design reviews, or attack-surface analysis.
Shows repeated, substantive assessment work with follow-through such as documented findings, remediation validation, or attacker-style code reading.

features.name: Security automation framing
features.description: How well the letter understands and is motivated by the role's core mission of scaling security work through automation and foundational security systems.

levels.descriptor: Interest in the role is generic and could fit many software jobs.
The letter shows some interest in security or backend impact, but the motivation stays broad.
The letter clearly wants to make secure behavior easier by default or reduce repetitive security toil.
The letter offers a nuanced philosophy of security automation as leverage, capacity creation, or quiet resilience.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: The presence and rigor of formal external security credentials or certifications.

levels.descriptor: No security credential is mentioned.
Mentions a foundational or introductory credential such as Security+ or an equivalent baseline certification.
Mentions a hands-on advanced credential such as OSCP or an equivalent practical certification.

features.name: Security mindset
features.description: Whether the letter conveys a thoughtful security-engineering philosophy or identity beyond generic interest or adjacent experience.

levels.descriptor: Security is mostly a keyword or destination, with little indication of how the applicant thinks about it.
Expresses sincere security interest, but methods or principles remain broad.
Explains a recognizable approach, such as threat modeling, attacker perspective, guardrails, or secure-by-default design.
Shows mature security judgment through multiple applied principles, such as bounded autonomy, adversarial thinking, design-level reasoning, or framing security as quiet resilience.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Direct experience building tooling that automates vulnerability intake, classification, routing, prioritization, deduplication, or related workflows.

levels.descriptor: No direct vulnerability-handling automation is described.
Shows general interest in automating security work, but no concrete triage example.
Gives a concrete example of building automation for vulnerability intake or report handling.
Shows clear ownership of triage automation and explains how it reduced manual work or improved flow.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: The surface professionalism of the letter's spelling, grammar, proofreading, and sentence-level cleanliness.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors, misspellings, or naming mistakes noticeably distract from the application.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the letter remains readable.
Mostly clean writing with only minor slips.
Polished, professional, and essentially error-free throughout.

other.name: Other
other.description: Miscellaneous low-recurring constructs that do not belong in the broader recurring criteria, such as language breadth or generic ownership and seniority signals.

levels.descriptor: Shows narrow breadth beyond the main language or two.
Shows moderate breadth across several additional languages.
Shows very broad breadth across many additional languages.
